- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast baseline or allow slight upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply a “cool-down” decay to forecast after peak.
- Model consistently overestimates in early forecast horizon (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply a downward bias to first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.5 to -1.0), model often fails to adjust quickly; introduce a “reversion buffer” to forecast, especially in 10–15 day window.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating +0.2 and -0.5); use sentiment-weighted average or median of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
